intro.TrustedMarkup:
A regular expression that searches, counts and replaces.

=~ only answers whether a whole string matches a constant pattern. The walk is Vyrn, not a builtin, so every engine runs one source and agrees on offsets and counts.

Supports literals, ., classes ([abc], [a-z], [^>]), alternation, grouping, * + ?, and \ escapes. A Thompson NFA with no backtracking, so the time is linear in the pattern size times the input for every pattern. A search runs it as a lazy DFA: one table read per byte. Refuses anchors, non-greedy repeats and counted repetition. It has no backreferences or lookaround: \1 is the byte 1.

Leftmost-longest (POSIX): a|ab against ab matches ab, where a backtracking engine answers a.

Offsets are bytes, and every match starts and ends on a character boundary: . and a negated class match one whole UTF-8 character. A class that lists a non-ASCII character is a set of its bytes.

sig.TrustedMarkup: type Regex = { op: Array<Int64>, a: Array<Int64>, b: Array<Int64>, cls: Array<ByteSet>, start: Int64, // `classOf[c]` is byte `c`'s class, 0 to `classCount - 1`: two bytes in one // class take the same step from every set of pcs. The class of `c` is at // most `c`, so a `UInt8` holds it. classOf: Array<UInt8>, classCount: Int64, }
type Match = { at: Int64, end: Int64 }

prose.TrustedMarkup: One match: a half-open byte range of the haystack.

sig.TrustedMarkup: fn compile(pattern: String) -> Result<Regex, String>

prose.TrustedMarkup: Compiles pattern, or says what is wrong with it. Compile once and search often: the whole cost of a pattern is paid here.

sig.TrustedMarkup: fn find(re: Regex, hay: String, from: Int64) -> Option<Match>

prose.TrustedMarkup: The first match at or after from, or None.

sig.TrustedMarkup: fn countMatches(re: Regex, hay: String) -> Int64

prose.TrustedMarkup: How many non-overlapping matches re has in hay: aa in aaa is one. An empty match advances by one byte.

sig.TrustedMarkup: fn replaceAll(re: Regex, hay: String, with: String) -> String

prose.TrustedMarkup: hay with every non-overlapping match replaced by with, taken literally: there are no captures, so no $1.
